## Verdict
- Answer: Fabrication depends on model, task and era. Peer-reviewed audits from 2023 to 2025 found 18–55% of generated citations did not exist in general-purpose chatbots without retrieval [r1][r4], and up to 91.4% for one weaker model on a systematic-review task [r3]. The newest audit I recall found 19.9% for GPT-4o [r4]. Even real citations often contain errors [r2][r4].
- Decision: Treat any unverified LLM-generated reference as untrustworthy. Require DOI or database verification before use, and do not set policy on a single "hallucination rate".
- Confidence: medium - several independent peer-reviewed audits agree on the order of magnitude, but they use different prompts, models and scoring. All figures here are from memory and no Prism calls were run.
- What would change it: Current audits (2026) of frontier models with web retrieval on a common benchmark, showing rates well below 5%.

## What the data shows
No Prism calls were run, so there are no [cN] numbers. Every figure below comes from a reference [rN] or is labelled (est.).

- **ChatGPT, general topics (2023).** GPT-3.5 fabricated 55% of citations and GPT-4 fabricated 18% [r1]. Among the non-fabricated citations, 43% (GPT-3.5) and 24% (GPT-4) had substantive errors [r1].
- **ChatGPT-3.5, medical references (2023).** Of 115 references, 47% were fabricated, 46% were authentic but inaccurate, and 7% were authentic and accurate [r2].
- **Systematic-review references (2024).** Hallucination rates were 39.6% for GPT-3.5, 28.6% for GPT-4 and 91.4% for Bard [r3].
- **GPT-4o on mental-health literature reviews (2025).** 19.9% of citations were fabricated [r4]. Of the real citations, 45.4% had bibliographic errors [r4]. Fabrication was higher for less-studied topics than for well-studied ones such as depression [r4].
- **Real-world incidents.** Deloitte Australia partly refunded a government report in October 2025 after fabricated references were found [r6]. Courts have sanctioned lawyers since *Mata v. Avianca* in 2023 [r5]. Public trackers of court filings with AI-fabricated citations passed several hundred cases by late 2025 (est.).
- **Conference papers.** GPTZero reported hundreds of hallucinated citations in accepted NeurIPS 2025 papers and ICLR 2026 submissions (est., unverified count).

**Facets I cannot measure:**
- Corpus volumes by lane (research vs news), because no search was run.
- Read/unread counts: I recall these studies from memory and have not read the full texts in this session, so all are "unread" in the strict sense.
- Any rate for 2026 models.
- A population-wide rate, because every audit uses a convenience prompt set.

## Trend
Fabricated-citation share across audits, 2023–2025. Tasks and models differ, so this is not a clean time series.


Within one study, moving from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4 cut fabrication from 55% to 18%, a 37-point drop [r1]. Across studies there is no clear decline: GPT-4 scored 18% [r1] and then 28.6% on a harder task [r3], and GPT-4o scored 19.9% [r4]. The data cannot say whether newer models fabricate less on a fixed task.

## Comparison
Baseline: the better model in each study, on that study's own task.

| Study | Worse model | Better model | Delta | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [r1] | GPT-3.5: 55% | GPT-4: 18% | 37 pts | 3.1x |
| [r3] | Bard: 91.4% | GPT-4: 28.6% | 62.8 pts | 3.2x |
| [r3] | GPT-3.5: 39.6% | GPT-4: 28.6% | 11 pts | 1.4x |

Ratios are computed from the cited figures.

## Evidence
Tier: all are peer-reviewed journal articles (tier A) except the news items (tier C). Quotes are unavailable because I did not retrieve texts; I do not reproduce quotes from memory.

- [r3] Chelli et al., JMIR, 2024. Supports the 39.6%, 28.6% and 91.4% rates. No verbatim quote.
- [r4] Linardon et al., JMIR Mental Health, 2025. Supports the 19.9% and 45.4% figures and the topic dependence. No verbatim quote.
- [r5] *Mata v. Avianca* (S.D.N.Y.), 2023, news and court coverage. Supports the existence of real-world harm.
- [r6] Deloitte Australia report refund, news, October 2025. Supports the incident.

**Contradicting or qualifying evidence:** I recall no study showing low fabrication for ungrounded chat models. Retrieval-grounded systems are the qualifier. They reduce invented references but still misattribute sources: a Tow Center/CJR 2025 test found AI search tools answered over 60% of news-citation queries incorrectly (est., unverified).

**Tier-weighted tally:** 4 tier-A studies support high rates, 0 contradict. This is a tally of studies I recall, not a systematic search.

## Method and limits
- **Windows:** the studies span 2023 to 2025. The latest audit I recall is from 2025, about 10+ months before today (2026-10-23), so the gap is roughly 10 months or more. Models since then are not covered.
- **Lanes:** research literature (peer-reviewed) and news (incidents). No corpus volumes were counted.
- **Coverage:** partial, from memory. DOIs were not verified.
- **Censoring:** published audits favour striking results. Papers on low rates may be missing.
- **Match mode:** "fabricated" means no matching real publication was found, but each study defines and checks this differently.
- **Counts are:** reported rates from specific prompt sets. **They are not:** general rates for all use, nor rates for retrieval-enabled products.
- **Interpretation:** the "no clear decline" reading and the decision advice are mine.
